questions.question: A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 250 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the car = 275 km

Time taken = 5 hours

Speed of the car = Distance / Time = 275 km / 5 hr = 55 km/h

New speed of the car = 55 km/h - 5 km/h = 50 km/h

Distance to be covered = 250 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

New time taken to cover 250 km at 50 km/h

⇒ Time = 250 km / 50 km/h

⇒ Time = 5 hours

**∴ The car will take 5 hours to cover 250 km.**

questions.question: Which of the following rules is used to determine the force on a current carrying conductor kept inside a magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fleming's left-hand rule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed inside a magnetic field.
 
• According to this rule, if you hold your left hand with the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger mutually perpendicular to each other, the thumb represents the direction of the force (motion), the forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger represents the direction of the current.
 
• This rule is particularly useful in motors where the direction of motion needs to be determined.
 
• It helps in understanding the relationship between the magnetic field, current, and the resulting force, which is crucial for designing and operating electric motors and generators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maxwell's corkscrew rule** is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• **Right hand thumb rule** is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field in a current-carrying conductor.
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• Both Fleming's rules (left-hand and right-hand) are essential for understanding electromagnetic induction and the functioning of electric motors and generators.

questions.question: A group of people contains men, women and children. If 40% of them are men, 35% are women and rest are children, and their average weights are 70 kg, 60 kg and 30 kg, respectively. The average weight of the group is:

questions.question: The focal length of a diverging lens is 50 cm. The power of the lens is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-2 D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Given: Focal length (f) = 50 cm = 0.50 m. As it's a diverging lens (concave lens), f = **–0.50 m**.
 
• Power (P) of lens is given by the formula: **P = 100/f (in cm)** or **P = 1/f (in m)**.
 
• Substituting: P = 1 / (–0.50) = **–2 dioptres (D)**.
 
• The negative sign indicates that it is a **concave (diverging)** lens.
 
• Therefore, the correct power of the lens is **–2 D**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power of a Lens:**

 
 
• It indicates the converging or diverging ability of a lens.
 
• Measured in **dioptres (D)**.
 
• 1 D = Power of a lens with focal length 1 metre.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens:**
 
 
• Also called a diverging lens.
 
• Forms virtual, erect, and diminished images.
 
• Has a **negative focal length** and **negative power**.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens:**
 
 
• Also called a converging lens.
 
• Has a **positive focal length** and **positive power**.
 
 
 
• **Lens Power Usage:**
 
 
• Used in corrective eyeglasses, microscopes, and cameras.
 
 
 
• **Unit Conversion:**
 
 
• To use power formula, focal length must be in metres (m).
 
• 1 cm = 0.01 m, hence 50 cm = 0.50 m.

questions.question: The current through horizontal straight wire flows from west to east. The direction of the magnetic field lines as viewed from the east end will be:

clockwise in a plane perpendicular to the wire
anticlockwise in the plane of the wire
clockwise in the plane of the wire

• The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor can be determined using the **right-hand thumb rule**.
 
• According to the rule, if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, the curl of your fingers shows the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• In this scenario, the current flows from west to east. When viewed from the east end, the magnetic field lines will appear to move in an **anticlockwise direction** in a plane perpendicular to the wire.
 
• This is because the fingers of your right hand will curl anticlockwise when the thumb points in the direction of the current (east).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the wire, and their direction depends on the direction of the current flow.
 
• This principle is crucial in the design and operation of electrical devices such as motors, generators, and transformers.

questions.question: Planets do not twinkle because

options.text: they act as extended source of light
they act as a point source of light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**they act as extended source of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Planets act as extended sources of light**, which means they cover a larger area in the sky compared to stars, which are point sources of light.
 
• This extended nature helps in averaging out the light coming from different parts of the planet, reducing the twinkling effect caused by atmospheric turbulence.
 
• Stars appear to twinkle because they are point sources of light, and atmospheric disturbances cause rapid changes in the light's path, making the stars appear to flicker.
 
• Planets, due to their larger apparent size, are less affected by these disturbances, and hence, they do not twinkle as stars do.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric turbulence** refers to the irregular motion of air caused by differences in temperature, pressure, and humidity in the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• This turbulence can bend the light from celestial objects, causing them to appear to move or flicker when observed from the Earth's surface.
 
• The phenomenon is more pronounced for objects that are point sources of light, such as stars, due to the smaller area they cover in the sky.
 
• Large telescopes and adaptive optics systems can help reduce the effect of atmospheric turbulence, providing clearer images of celestial objects.

questions.question: If d² + (1)/(d²) = 18, and d > (1)/(d) then the value of d³ - (1)/(d³) is :

Let x = d + (1/d)

questions.question: The total surface area of a cylinder of diameter 10 cm is 330 square centimeters. Find the height of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total surface area of the cylinder = 330 cm²

Diameter of the cylinder = 10 cm

Radius (r) = Diameter / 2 = 10 / 2 = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

Total surface area of a cylinder = 2πr(h + r)

**Calculation:**

330 = 2π × 5 × (h + 5)

⇒ 330 = 10π(h + 5)

⇒ 330 / 10π = h + 5

⇒ 33 / π = h + 5

⇒ h = 33 / π - 5

Using π ≈ 3.14:

⇒ h ≈ 33 / 3.14 - 5

⇒ h ≈ 10.5 - 5

⇒ h ≈ 5.5

**∴ The height of the cylinder is 5.5 cm**

• **Statement II:** The effective nuclear charge acting on the valence shell electrons increases across a period, the tendency to lose electrons will decrease.
 
• Both statements are correct. As we move from left to right across a period, elements tend to gain electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration, hence their metallic character decreases. ***Therefore, Statement I is correct.***
 
• The effective nuclear charge (the net positive charge experienced by valence electrons) increases across a period due to the increase in the number of protons in the nucleus. This makes it harder for the elements to lose electrons, explaining the decrease in metallic character. ***Therefore, Statement II is correct and it explains Statement I.***
 
• **Hence, the correct answer is option 2.**
